amendmentLines.text: After Clause 117, insert the following new Clause—
“Review of public service pension schemes

The Secretary of State must, within 12 months of the day on which this Act is passed, conduct and publish a review of the long-term affordability, intergenerational fairness, fiscal sustainability, and accounting treatment of public service pension schemes.
In conducting the review under subsection (1), the Secretary of State must have regard to—
the current and projected cost to the Exchequer of such schemes,
their affordability in the context of long-term public finances,
the impact of such schemes on different generations of taxpayers and scheme members,
the implications of demographic change, including longevity and workforce participation, for the sustainability of such schemes, and
the manner in which the liabilities associated with such schemes are recorded, disclosed, and accounted for within the public sector balance sheet and related fiscal reporting frameworks.
In preparing the review, the Secretary of State must consult—
the Office for Budget Responsibility,
the National Audit Office,
His Majesty’s Treasury, and
such other persons or bodies as the Secretary of State considers appropriate.
The schemes to which subsection (1) applies are—
the NHS Pension Scheme,
the Teachers’ Pension Scheme,
the Civil Service Pension Scheme,
the Armed Forces Pension Scheme,
the Police Pension Scheme,
the Firefighters’ Pension Scheme, and
any other public service pension scheme designated by the Treasury by regulations as operating on an unfunded or pay-as-you-go basis.
The review must be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
Nothing in this section affects any pension entitlement accrued in respect of service.”

explanatoryText: This new clause would require the Secretary of State to conduct and publish a review of the long-term affordability, intergenerational fairness, fiscal sustainability, and accounting treatment of public service pension schemes.
decisionExplanation: This amendment was agreed to. Where a member has given notice of their intention to oppose a Clause/Schedule standing part of a Bill, 'agreed' indicates that the Clause/Schedule was removed from the Bill.
